name: Rwandan Nationality by Origin (Descent), and Foundling/Statelessness Grounds

qualifying_event.description: A person born to at least one parent who is Rwandan 'by origin' (i.e. Rwandan by ancestry, not by acquisition) has Rwandan nationality by origin, per the Organic Law N 002/2021.OL governing Rwandan Nationality. Establishing this where formal documentation is unavailable requires testimony from Rwandan blood relatives.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth record from the country of birth; documentation confirming the parent's Rwandan-by-origin status; where direct documentary proof is unavailable, testimony from three Rwandan blood relatives as witnesses.

requirements.blocker_text: At least one parent is Rwandan by origin (by ancestry, not by acquired/naturalised citizenship).

Where formal documentation of Rwandan-by-origin parentage is unavailable, testimony corroborated by three Rwandan blood relatives, or another relative with Rwandan nationality by origin, may substitute.
Found as a child in Rwanda with parents unknown, or would otherwise be stateless -- both independently named grounds under the 2021 Organic Law.

evidence_required.document: Birth record from country of birth
Testimony of 3 Rwandan blood relatives (where documentation is unavailable)

sources.title: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration (DGIE), Rwanda -- citizenship by origin: at least one Rwandan-by-origin parent, birth record from country of birth, documentation of parental ancestry, or three Rwandan blood-relative witnesses where documentation is unavailable

Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative (NGO tracking African nationality law) -- Organic Law N 002/2021.OL of 16/07/2021: foundling status and statelessness listed as independently named acquisition grounds alongside 'by origin' descent

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Rwanda). STATUS: DRAFT -- the descent-specific requirements (standard and witness-based groups) are tier-1 DGIE sourced, but the foundling/statelessness group cites the tier-3 NGO-hosted law summary only (their existence as separate grounds is confirmed there but not independently corroborated on a tier-1 page in this pass); since this dataset requires ALL hard requirements to be tier-1 for published status, the whole file stays draft rather than being split awkwardly across statuses. THE THREE-BLOOD-RELATIVE-WITNESS REQUIREMENT is a genuinely distinctive evidentiary mechanism not seen elsewhere in this dataset -- it reflects the practical reality that formal civil documentation is not universally available for establishing ancestry, and Rwanda's law builds an alternative evidentiary path around community/family testimony rather than requiring paper records that may not exist. This is disclosed as a notable structural feature, not just a procedural footnote.
